title: Ketamine for depression: clinical issues and mechanisms.
abstract: Ketamine is a high-affinity N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist. Clinical trials have demonstrated that subanesthetic intravenous infusion of ketamine produces rapid, robust, and sustained antidepressant effects in patients suffering from treatment-resistant major depression and endogenous depression. The therapeutic mechanism involves blockade of NMDA receptors (GRIN1 and GRIN2A) on GABAergic interneurons, leading to a burst of glutamate transmission, activation of AMPA receptors, and rapid release of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). This initiates mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling and synaptogenesis in the prefrontal cortex, effectively reversing synaptic deficits associated with chronic depression.

title: NMDA receptor regulation by ketamine in refractory depression.
abstract: Major depressive disorder is a debilitating illness. Traditional monoaminergic antidepressants targeting serotonin and norepinephrine take weeks to achieve therapeutic response. Ketamine exhibits rapid antidepressant actions by antagonizing glutamate NMDA receptor subunits GRIN1 and GRIN2A. Inhibition of spontaneous NMDA receptor miniature neurotransmission deactivates eukaryotic elongation factor 2 kinase, leading to desuppression of BDNF translation and synaptic potentiation. These molecular events alleviate depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation.

title: Synaptic mechanisms of ketamine's antidepressant action.
abstract: Ketamine, originally used as an anesthetic, represents a paradigm shift in psychiatric therapeutics. In patients with endogenous depression, ketamine induces rapid synaptogenesis and increases spine density in cortical neurons. This action is mediated by antagonism of NMDA receptor complex, up-regulation of BDNF, and enhancement of synaptic connectivity, demonstrating therapeutic efficacy distinct from serotonin transporter inhibitors.

title: Low-dose colchicine for secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease.
abstract: Inflammation plays an essential role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease. Colchicine is a classical anti-inflammatory medication long prescribed for acute gout. In the prospective randomized LoDoCo trial, addition of low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg daily) to standard secondary prevention therapies significantly reduced the risk of acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction in patients with stable coronary artery disease. Colchicine inhibits microtubule assembly, impairs leukocyte extravasation, and suppresses the NLRP3 inflammasome, leading to marked reductions in interleukin-1beta (IL1B) and C-reactive protein levels.

title: Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome with colchicine in atherosclerosis.
abstract: Atherosclerosis is driven by cholesterol crystal-induced activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome within arterial macrophages, promoting secretion of interleukin-1beta and vascular plaque destabilization. Colchicine selectively suppresses microtubule polymerization and attenuates NLRP3 activation in human monocytes. In clinical evaluations of coronary artery disease, colchicine therapy reduces local cardiac production of inflammatory cytokines and stabilizes vulnerable atherosclerotic plaques, demonstrating cardiorenal protective benefits beyond lipid lowering.

title: Anti-inflammatory therapy with colchicine for coronary plaque stabilization.
abstract: Chronic inflammation contributes directly to coronary artery disease and plaque rupture. Colchicine reduces neutrophil extracellular traps and inhibits inflammatory cascades mediated by IL1B and TNF-alpha. Administration of colchicine in patients with coronary artery disease and atherosclerosis leads to favorable plaque remodeling and lower cardiovascular mortality.

title: Cardiovascular and renal benefits of SGLT2 inhibitor dapagliflozin.
abstract: Dapagliflozin is a selective inhibitor of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SLC5A2) expressed in the proximal renal tubules. Beyond lowering plasma glucose, dapagliflozin promotes osmotic diuresis, reduces blood pressure and arterial stiffness, and decreases cardiac preload and afterload. These hemodynamic actions alleviate myocardial wall stress in heart failure and dilated cardiomyopathy. Furthermore, dapagliflozin reduces intraglomerular pressure, attenuating hyperfiltration and progression of chronic kidney failure.

title: Renal and cardiac protection with dapagliflozin.
abstract: Inhibition of SLC5A2 by dapagliflozin delivers profound renoprotective actions by restoring tubuloglomerular feedback, decreasing glomerular hyperfiltration, and reducing albuminuria in chronic kidney failure. In the cardiovascular system, dapagliflozin alters myocardial substrate utilization from glucose to ketone bodies, improving cardiac efficiency and mitigating progression to dilated cardiomyopathy.

title: A randomized, controlled trial of 3.0 mg of liraglutide in weight management.
abstract: Obesity is a chronic progressive disease with limited pharmacotherapeutic options. Liraglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that shares 97% sequence homology with human GLP-1. In the SCALE trial, once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide 3.0 mg in conjunction with lifestyle intervention produced significant, sustained weight loss in patients with obesity. Liraglutide activates GLP-1 receptors (GLP1R) in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus, enhancing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons and suppressing neuropeptide Y (NPY) signaling, which decreases appetite, reduces energy intake, and delays gastric emptying.

title: Central mechanisms of GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide in obesity.
abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) is widely expressed in both peripheral pancreatic islets and central nervous system regions regulating energy homeostasis. Peripheral administration of liraglutide accesses circumventricular organs and the hypothalamus. Activation of central GLP1R increases satiety and reduces food reward behavior, leading to meaningful therapeutic reduction in adiposity and body weight in individuals with obesity.
